sn42.12:1.1: Nothing further is known of this chief. His name means “heaper”, perhaps in reference to the wealth that is heaped up and the suffering that is worn away.
sn42.12:2.1: The Buddha repeats the opening of the First Sermon ([sn56.11]()). The text goes on to illustrate these two extremes and the middle way. The lengthy explanation suggests that Rāsiya was slow of understanding.
sn42.12:3.1: This is the first extreme, sensual indulgence. A similar analysis is at [an10.91]().
sn42.12:16.1: This is the second extreme, self mortification.
sn42.12:22.1: Here is the middle way, described as a “wearing away” (_nijjara_). This is a Jain term ([mn14:17.5]()) adapted for Buddhist use. It is applied to the tenfold path at [an10.106]().
